title: Decision register: what we know, what we do not, and what to do about it
purpose: A decision is only reasonable once the question, the evidence we already hold and the gap in that evidence are all written down. This register does that for every open decision. Nothing here is approved - it is a review queue.
rules: Every 'information we have' cell carries a link to the official source or names the measured artefact in data/derived/.
Every 'information we do not have' cell is left blank in the underlying data, never estimated.
Every gap has at least one suggested way to close it, naming the official source that would close it.

questions.question: Can my own lines beat the closing market line?
questions.have: No. Measured over 4,055 games (2011-2026), the correlation between (own line - market line) and the actual result against the market spread is r = 0.0072, 95% CI [-0.024, 0.038], p = 0.65. Mean absolute error: own 10.56 vs market 10.01 on the spread; own 10.77 vs market 10.43 on the total.
questions.have_source: https://www.nfl.com/scores/2026/REG9 (official scores used to verify the archive) and data/derived/correlations.json entries CR-01 to CR-06
questions.gap: Nothing in the public data used here (final scores, rest, starter QB, venue) separates my line from the closing line. The market is better informed than this model on every measured axis.
questions.decidable_now: Yes - the answer is no, on this evidence.
questions.action: Do not fund any strategy on the current model. Re-measure only after an information source the market prices late is added (see Q02, Q03, Q05).

questions.question: Should injury and depth information be part of the model?
questions.have: Yes, and it is already collected. NFL.com publishes an official injury report per game with Player / Position / Injury / Practice Status / Game Status. All 14 Week 10 games were transcribed (275 player rows) into data/official/injuries_week10_2026.json.
questions.gap: The model does not consume it. The Week 10 MIA @ IND total shows why: the market total is 38.5, the model's is 46.68 (an 8.18-point gap) and the official news on the same page says Miami placed QB Malik Willis on injured reserve with Kyle McCord in line for his first start. The model has no idea a first-time starter is playing.
questions.decidable_now: No - the pipeline exists but is not wired in.
questions.action: Add the official injury report as a model feature, starting with the single highest-value one: whether the club's most-used QB earlier in the season is the named starter. Both inputs are official (https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ and the starter names in the game archive).

questions.question: Can we identify 2nd, 3rd and 4th string replacements for injured starters?
questions.have: No. The official injury report gives position and status but never a depth-chart rank.
questions.gap: Depth rank. Without it, 'a 3rd-string cornerback is replacing a starter' cannot be distinguished from 'a starter is questionable but practising fully'. Every depth-rank cell on the site is blank by design.
questions.action: Source an official depth chart. NFL.com team pages are the natural place to look; this session did not find an official, machine-readable depth-chart endpoint, so the requirement is logged as an open acquisition item rather than filled with a guess.

questions.question: Does the market misprice same-game parlays through correlation?
questions.have: Measured correlation between 'home covers' and 'over' is r = 0.0083, 95% CI [-0.023, 0.040], p = 0.60 (n = 3,912). Between 'favourite covers' and 'over' it is r = -0.0167, 95% CI [-0.048, 0.015], p = 0.30 (n = 3,908). Both include zero.
questions.gap: Correlations for the specific legs a sportsbook actually offers (player props, team totals, alternate lines). Those legs have no verifiable price history in any source available here.
questions.decidable_now: Partially - for side+total legs the answer is that the independence assumption is close enough; for player-prop legs it is unknowable with current data.
questions.action: Keep the empirical-joint-probability pricer (strategy C-SGP-FAV-OVER) rather than assuming independence, and extend it only when a verifiable prop price history exists.

questions.question: Are we measuring against the right price: closing line or the line we could actually bet?
questions.have: Only closing lines. The archive stores one spread, one total and one moneyline per game with the prices attached.
questions.have_source: data/raw/nfldata_games.csv (third-party archive; the NFL publishes no official odds)
questions.gap: Opening lines, line movement, and the time at which each price was available. If the model's edge only exists against an opening number that is long gone, every ROI here is overstated.
questions.action: Acquire a timestamped line history. No official NFL source exists; this is a commercial data purchase decision and is logged as such rather than assumed away.

questions.question: Is any observed return skill or luck?
questions.have: Measured, not asserted. Each strategy carries a 20,000-trial no-skill simulation at its own prices, giving a 95% ROI band. The best strategy by ROI, S-WIND-UNDER, returned +7.77% over 303 bets against a no-skill band of [-11.08%, +10.82%] - inside the band, p = 0.17, and p = 0.44 after Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all 15 strategies.
questions.gap: Sample size. At these win rates, detecting a 3-point edge at -110 with 80% power needs thousands of bets; no strategy here comes close.
questions.decidable_now: Yes - on this evidence, no strategy has demonstrated skill.
questions.action: Hold rewards until a strategy clears the gates. Report the required sample size alongside every result so the gap is explicit.

questions.question: How should multiple strategies be judged at once?
questions.have: A policy exists and is applied: Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction across all strategies at q = 0.05, plus a pre-declared confirmation period (2022-2026) that was never used for design.
questions.gap: Nothing material. This is the one area where the process is already complete.
questions.action: Keep the policy and apply it to any future strategy before it is added to the leaderboard.

questions.question: Is there an official NFL source for betting lines?
questions.have: No. The NFL does not publish official odds, spreads or totals. Everything on this site labelled 'market' comes from a third-party archive and is labelled as such everywhere it appears.
questions.have_source: https://www.nfl.com/ (official league site - no odds published)
questions.gap: An official price source. It does not exist.
questions.decidable_now: Yes - the gap is permanent and must be disclosed, not filled.
questions.action: Keep the third-party label on every market number. Never present a market line as verified fact.

questions.question: Is the historical archive trustworthy?
questions.have: Partly verified. Three complete 2026 weeks (1, 8 and 9 - 45 games) were re-read directly from NFL.com score pages and compared game by game: 45 of 45 final scores match exactly. Seven structural integrity checks also pass, including a full recomputation of W/L/T/PF/PA for all 32 teams from the game log against the official standings table.
questions.gap: Weeks outside 1, 8 and 9 of 2026, and every season before 2026, were not re-read page by page. Week 5 of 2026 could not be checked at all: the official page rendered every score as the literal text 'Hidden Score'.
questions.action: Extend the spot-check to one week per season before any result is treated as settled, and record the 'Hidden Score' rendering as an irregularity (IR-01).

questions.question: What should be staked, and by whom?
questions.have: Nothing is staked. Every figure on this site is in paper units at 1 unit per bet, and no money has been committed.
questions.gap: Bankroll size, risk tolerance, Kelly vs flat staking, and who authorises a real bet. None of these has been supplied.
questions.action: Supply a bankroll policy before any strategy leaves the lab. Until then the leaderboard scores skill, not money.

questions.question: Should playoff and international games be modelled the same way?
questions.have: The evaluation universe is regular-season games only (game_type = REG). Neutral-site games are handled: the home-field term is switched off when the location field is not 'Home'.
questions.gap: Playoff behaviour is unmeasured. International kickoff times and travel are unmodelled.
questions.action: Either exclude playoffs explicitly (current behaviour) or model them separately. Do not silently mix them.

questions.question: Is the rest / bye-week term in the model too strong?
questions.have: The fitted coefficient is 0.71 points of home margin per day of rest differential, applied linearly. For Week 10 PIT @ CIN, Pittsburgh's bye (14 days vs 7) produces a 4.9-point swing, which is what flips the model's line 7.06 points away from the market.
questions.gap: A defensible functional form. The linear term is a pre-registered simplification, not an established finding, and the bye case is exactly where a linear term is least credible.
questions.action: Re-specify rest as a categorical feature (short week / normal / bye) and re-register the parameters before the next run. Do not adjust the coefficient to make this week's line look better.

questions.question: Which data rights apply to the archive?
questions.have: The archive is a third-party GitHub repository, pinned to a commit and recorded with its download URL in data/provenance.json. It is used for research in a public repository.
questions.gap: A licence review. The repository's own terms were not read line by line in this session.
questions.action: Read the repository's licence and data terms before any commercial use. Logged as irregularity IR-05.

questions.question: Does the model know the weather?
questions.have: Wind, temperature, roof and surface are in the archive, and one strategy uses wind (>= 15 mph outdoors, unders: +7.77% over 303 bets, inside the no-skill band).
questions.gap: The weather values are not verified against an official or meteorological source, so a strategy built on them rests on unverified inputs.
questions.action: Either verify the archive's weather fields against a primary source or mark every weather-derived figure unverified. Currently marked unverified.

questions.question: What is the leaderboard actually rewarding?
questions.have: A z-score of the observed win rate against the break-even rate implied by the prices actually taken - not raw ROI, which would simply rank luck. Zero strategies are currently reward-eligible because none clears all eight gates.
questions.gap: The reward itself. No prize, stake or payout has been defined or funded.
questions.decidable_now: Partially - the ranking rule is settled; the reward is not.
questions.action: Define the reward before the first eligible strategy appears, so the incentive cannot be retro-fitted to whoever happens to be winning.

questions.question: Can this dashboard tell whether a current-week line is already stale or past kickoff?
questions.have: The frozen snapshot says it was retrieved at 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z. On 2026-11-13, NFL.com marked Washington–New York 24–21, Final, while the own-lines output still included that matchup as an upcoming forecast.
questions.gap: There is no live refresh, per-game status invalidation, or visible stale-snapshot warning in the data pipeline. The weekly snapshot can therefore continue displaying a line after kickoff or after a result is final.
questions.decidable_now: Yes - the observed stale-line case is verified; refresh and invalidation are proposed, not implemented.
questions.action: Before publishing or exposing any line as actionable, compare it with the current official schedule/scores, exclude games at or beyond kickoff and those marked final, display source-retrieval and model-as-of timestamps, and fail closed when the official game state cannot be verified.

suggestions.suggestion: Feed the official injury report into the forecast, starting with one feature: whether the club's most-used QB earlier in the season is the named starter.
suggestions.why: The single largest own-line disagreement in Week 10 (MIA @ IND, 8.18 points on the total) sits on a game where the official page states Miami's QB is on injured reserve and a first-time starter is in line.
suggestions.success_test: CR-01 (edge vs result) confidence interval moves away from zero, measured only on games after the feature is added.

suggestions.suggestion: Acquire an official depth-chart source so 2nd/3rd/4th-string replacements can be identified.
suggestions.why: The requirement 'know any deficiencies such as 2nd, 3rd or 4th string backups having to replace starters' cannot be met from the injury report alone - it has no depth rank.
suggestions.success_test: At least 90% of Week 10 players on the official injury report have an official depth rank attached.

suggestions.suggestion: Acquire timestamped opening and closing lines so every edge is measured against a price that actually existed when the bet could be placed.
suggestions.why: Right now the model can only be measured against a closing line it has no hope of beating, which makes the whole evaluation pessimistic but also unverifiable in the optimistic direction.
suggestions.evidence: No official source exists; this is a commercial purchase.
suggestions.success_test: Every graded bet carries both an opening and a closing price with timestamps.

suggestions.suggestion: Replace the linear rest term with a categorical short-week / normal / bye feature and re-register the parameters before the next run.
suggestions.why: A linear 0.71 points per day produces a 4.9-point bye effect, which is the main driver of the largest spread disagreement in Week 10.
suggestions.success_test: Re-registered parameter file committed before the next run; the bye effect is reported as a fitted category, not a slope.

suggestions.suggestion: Extend the official score spot-check from 3 weeks of 2026 to one week per season across the whole evaluation window.
suggestions.why: The archive is trusted on 45 games. The other 4,010 are unverified against a primary source.
suggestions.evidence: https://www.nfl.com/scores/2026/REG9 pattern applies to every season and week
suggestions.success_test: At least one full week per season, every season, re-read from NFL.com with a published match rate.

suggestions.suggestion: Publish the decision register as the entry point to the site, above the model output.
suggestions.why: Right now the most valuable content on the site is the list of things we do not know. Burying it under a table of lines inverts the value.
suggestions.success_test: The register is reachable in one click from the landing page - done.

suggestions.suggestion: Require every submitted strategy to declare its parameters in a file committed BEFORE its first run, and reject any strategy whose parameters were changed after results were seen.
suggestions.why: This is the only mechanism that separates a strategy from a curve fit. It is already applied to the house model (data/model_params.json carries a registration timestamp).
suggestions.success_test: Every leaderboard row links to a parameter file whose commit precedes its first result.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a player-prop module, but publish no numbers until a verifiable prop price history exists.
suggestions.why: The engine for prop combinations is specified here, but the NFL publishes no prop lines and no verifiable prop archive was available to this session, so every prop cell is blank by design.
suggestions.success_test: A prop strategy appears on the leaderboard with a sourced price for every leg.

suggestions.suggestion: Automate the weekly pipeline: fetch the official schedule, injury report and standings, regenerate the lines, re-run the gates, and publish - without manual input.
suggestions.why: Today the official pages are read and transcribed by hand. That does not scale past one week and introduces transcription risk.
suggestions.success_test: A scheduled run produces the Week 11 page with no human step.

suggestions.suggestion: Verify or drop the archive's weather fields.
suggestions.why: The best-performing strategy on the board is built entirely on an unverified wind field.
suggestions.success_test: Weather fields matched to a primary source, or the wind strategy removed from the board.

suggestions.suggestion: Consolidate the eleven overlapping NFL namespaces in this repository behind one canonical site, or publish an explicit index stating which one is authoritative.
suggestions.why: The repository contains nfl/, nfl-lab/, nfl-quant/, nfl-research/, nfl-decisions/ and this one. A reader cannot tell which is authoritative.
suggestions.success_test: One NFL namespace is declared canonical and the others are either removed or explicitly archived in the README.

suggestions.suggestion: Define and fund the leaderboard reward before any strategy becomes eligible.
suggestions.why: Choosing a prize after seeing who is winning invites gaming the metric.
suggestions.success_test: A written reward schedule exists and is committed before the first eligible strategy.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a hard freshness and kickoff gate before publishing current-week lines.
suggestions.why: NFL.com now marks Washington–New York final (24–21), but the dashboard still publishes that game as an upcoming line. A static snapshot needs an explicit as-of label and must never make a post-kickoff line look actionable.
suggestions.success_test: The pipeline refreshes and records official-source retrieval times; every line is blocked once kickoff begins or the official score page says Final; stale or unverifiable game status fails closed; pages show their as-of timestamp and explicit stale warning.
